problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $t=2$, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(2) & =\frac{1}{3}⟨2,-1,2⟩, \\ N(2) & =\frac{1}{3}⟨-1,2,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating a Specific Binormal Vector to a Curve Given the Unit Tangent and Principal Normal
examples.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $\mathbf r(t)$ at the point $t=\pi$, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\pi ) & =\frac{1}{5}⟨0,-3,4⟩, \\ N(\pi ) & =⟨1,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $\mathbf T$ and $\mathbf N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
examples.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
\mathbf B(t) = \mathbf T(t) \times \mathbf N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(\pi ) & =T(\pi )\times N(\pi ) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨0,-3,4⟩\times ⟨1,0,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & -3 & 4 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨(0-0),-(0-4),(0-(-3))⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨0,4,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at an arbitrary point, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}⟨0,{e}^{t},1⟩, \\ N(t) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}⟨0,1,-{e}^{t}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
feedback.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(t) & =T(t)\times N(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}⟨0,{e}^{t},1⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+1}}⟨0,1,-{e}^{t}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{2t}+1}\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & {e}^{t} & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -{e}^{t}\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{2t}+1}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & 1 \\ 1 & -{e}^{t}\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & -{e}^{t}\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}0 & {e}^{t} \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{2t}+1}⟨-{e}^{2t}-1,-(0-0),0-0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{2t}+1}⟨-({e}^{2t}+1),0,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
